blocks.title: Commercial Engine
blocks.body: Tribute Portfolio commercial distribution rides Marriott Bonvoy direct channels, GDS, OTAs, and parent sales systems. Independent-spirited soft collection: distinctive hotels with local character plus Marriott Bonvoy commercial systems—without collapsing into a hard-brand prototype. Owners should underwrite channel mix and loyalty contribution for this asset—not corporate averages alone.

blocks.title: Commercial Differentiator
blocks.body: Versus Autograph's often more design-led upper-upscale to luxury-leaning character hotels, Tribute Portfolio spans independent upper-upscale conversions with soft-collection flexibility inside Bonvoy.

blocks.title: Channels
blocks.body: Brand.com / Marriott Bonvoy app · major OTAs · GDS · metasearch (where active for the hotel)

blocks.title: Campaigns
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy and parent portfolio campaigns where the hotel is eligible

blocks.title: B2B Programs

blocks.title: Distribution & Channel Mix
blocks.body: Parent central reservations, Marriott Bonvoy app, and designated online channels—confirm commission structures and rate parity obligations in the current agreement exhibit.

blocks.body: Parent revenue tools and Marriott Bonvoy demand signals support pricing experiments; owners still need property-level strategy for this brand's product promise.

blocks.title: Digital Marketing & Performance Media
blocks.body: Paid and owned media templates at portfolio scale, with creative that must still feel brand- and hotel-specific rather than generic parent advertising.

blocks.title: Corporate, SME & Group Pull
blocks.body: Contracted travelers, small meetings, and negotiated programs where Tribute Portfolio fits the account's brand ladder.

blocks.title: Owner Perception Risk
blocks.body: Owners sometimes expect lifestyle lightness without systems cost; Tribute Portfolio still carries parent systems, Marriott Bonvoy economics, and brand QA. Align IC expectations early.

blocks.title: Marriott Bonvoy
blocks.body: Tribute Portfolio participates in Marriott Bonvoy. Members earn and redeem points and receive Elite recognition across participating sister brands. Confirm current tier names and earn rules on the official program site before IC.

blocks.title: Loyalty
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy at Tribute Portfolio

blocks.title: Earn
blocks.body: Guests earn Marriott Bonvoy points on qualifying stays at Tribute Portfolio. Elite members may receive enhanced earn and recognition benefits per current program rules.

blocks.title: Redeem
blocks.body: Points redeem for stays across the Marriott Bonvoy portfolio, including Tribute Portfolio, subject to availability and current redemption charts.

blocks.title: Elite Recognition
blocks.body: Elite status recognition (upgrades, late checkout, lounge access where offered) applies per property capability—delivery varies by hotel.

blocks.title: Ecosystem
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy partnerships, co-branded cards, and bonus campaigns expand the loyalty halo; Tribute Portfolio stays remain the property-level earn/redeem node.

blocks.title: Owner Lens
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy drives distribution and repeat demand but adds loyalty chargebacks and program economics. Underwrite net contribution after loyalty—not membership vanity metrics.

blocks.title: P&L Implications
blocks.body: Loyalty assessments and program contribution affect net rooms revenue. Use current agreement exhibits; do not invent undisclosed rates.

blocks.title: Operating Implications
blocks.body: Front desk and systems must support Marriott Bonvoy enrollment, Elite recognition, and redemption stays without erasing the brand's guest experience.

blocks.title: Systems Implications
blocks.body: Parent property and reservation systems integration is required for Marriott Bonvoy participation—budget cutover and training in the conversion plan.

blocks.title: Repeat Guest Capture
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy earn and recognition increase the probability of repeat Tribute Portfolio stays where the hotel already competes on product fit—not on a standardized prototype alone.

blocks.title: Direct Channel & Member Pricing
blocks.body: Bonvoy member rates and Marriott direct paths help Tribute Portfolio hotels defend contribution against high-commission intermediaries while keeping brand positioning intact.

blocks.title: Elite Member Value
blocks.body: Elite recognition (upgrades where available, late checkout, milestone rewards) supports contribution at Tribute Portfolio; amenity delivery still varies by property capability.

blocks.title: Cross-Brand Traveler Flow
blocks.body: Bonvoy recognition across Marriott sister brands matters for guests who split stays within the network—Tribute Portfolio remains the brand-specific node inside that earn/redeem graph.

blocks.title: Cobrand & Payment Scale
blocks.body: Bonvoy co-branded cards, Moments, and bonus-point campaigns lift acquisition; model hotel-level contribution after loyalty chargebacks—not portfolio vanity metrics.

blocks.title: Corporate & Small Meetings
blocks.body: Marriott account linkage and negotiated transient patterns support midweek compression where corporate and SMERF mix fits the Tribute Portfolio asset—confirm for this hotel's source markets.

blocks.title: To Operate

blocks.title: When Things Change
blocks.body: Renewal PIP; conversion PIP revisions; transfer / change-of-ownership fees; termination-related obligations; owner-funded reserves—triggered at renewal, repositioning, or exit. Confirm liquidated damages and transfer mechanics in the current agreement.

blocks.title: Fee Variability
blocks.body: Initial vs conversion paths differ; program contribution and loyalty assessments may change by year under agreement terms. Lock the fee exhibit before IC—never extrapolate from a peer hotel's rumor. Geography note: Confirm current Marriott franchise / development disclosure for Tribute Portfolio

blocks.title: Why Value Is Strongest in These Scenarios
blocks.body:
Keep Local Product Intent—Add Marriott Bonvoy: retain Tribute Portfolio's brand promise while accessing loyalty earn/redeem and parent commercial systems a standalone hotel cannot buy alone.
Independent-spirited soft collection: distinctive hotels with local character plus Marriott Bonvoy commercial systems—without collapsing into a hard-brand prototype.
Sibling Clarity: diligence fit versus same-parent peers before assuming identical owner use case or fee path.
Operator & Owner Fit: strongest when the asset can deliver the brand's guest promise with QA discipline—weakest when sponsors want the flag without the product investment.
Disclosure Discipline: model economics only from current fee exhibits—Factory 2.0 does not invent undisclosed percentages.

blocks.title: Independent Character Conversion
blocks.body: Distinctive independents that want Marriott Bonvoy without erasing hotel individuality into a hard Marriott prototype.

blocks.title: Landmark & Adaptive Reuse
blocks.body: Heritage and adaptive-reuse assets where architecture and sense of place are the product—pair design capital with Bonvoy systems.

blocks.title: Sibling Clarity Versus Autograph
blocks.body: Assets that fit soft-collection economics but need diligence against Autograph and Design Hotels before assuming the same owner use case or fee path.
